bibliographic.title: A machine learning model to predict the risk of 30-day readmissions in patients with heart failure: a retrospective analysis of electronic medical records data
bibliographic.journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

study_design.outcome: 30-day hospital readmission in heart failure patients

model.selection_criterion: comparison of DUNs, gradient boosting, logistic regression, maxout networks
model.feature_selection_method: structured (demographics, labs) + NLP from clinical notes
model.preprocessing_pipeline: NLP feature extraction likely on full data

leakage_risk_assessment.notes: LIKELY PATIENT-LEVEL LEAKAGE. 10-fold CV with 27,334 admissions from 11,510 patients — patients with multiple admissions could appear in both train and test folds. NLP preprocessing likely on full data. No calibration. SD from CV folds instead of bootstrap CI. No temporal validation. Modest AUC (0.705).

reviewer_notes.notes: METHODOLOGICAL ISSUES. Likely patient-level leakage in CV folds (27K admissions from 11K patients). No calibration, no CI. MLGG should flag split_protocol_gate (patient overlap), leakage_gate, calibration_dca_gate.
